    c = Counter(s)
    return [ch for ch in s if c[ch] == 1]

title: Lexicographical Permutations of a String
statement: Generate all unique permutations of string s in lexicographically sorted order.
hint1: Sort the characters initially.
hint2: Use backtracking or next_permutation, and deduplicate identical branches.

solution.python:
def solve(s):
    res = []
    chars = sorted(list(s))
    used = [False] * len(chars)
    def backtrack(path):
        if len(path) == len(chars):
            res.append(''.join(path))
            return
        for i in range(len(chars)):
            if used[i]: continue
            if i > 0 and chars[i] == chars[i-1] and not used[i-1]: continue
            used[i] = True
            path.append(chars[i])
            backtrack(path)
            path.pop()
            used[i] = False
    backtrack([])
    return res
